topics.title: Round sequence & Supply
topics.html:
The holder of the First Player Marker chooses who acts first at the start of each phase. Players then alternate unit activations. An activation and an action are different: an activation can contain allowed abilities around its normal action. [RB §§8.1-8.4, pp. 54-56; §10.2, p. 79]

Phase Procedure
1. Movement Resolve Start of the Round effects, holder first; establish Supply. Activate units for Move, Deploy, Disengage or Hold.
2. Assault Activate eligible on-table units for Ranged Attack, Charge, Run or Hold; obey Disengage restrictions.
3. Combat Alternate engaged units for Close Combat Attacks; they must activate. Close Ranks is optional within that action.
4. Scoring & Cleanup Determine control -> score VP simultaneously -> end-game check -> End of the Round effects -> cleanup/refresh -> next initiative.

[RB §§8.3-8.9, pp. 55-72]

In Phases 1 and 2, place activation markers and give the First Player Marker for the next phase to the first player to pass. Passing ends that player's participation in the phase; mark remaining units so they cannot act, but they have not actually activated or performed Hold. Hold is a real action. A zero-distance Move/Run is Hold. During Combat, pass only once no engaged units remain eligible; remove their activation markers after their Combat activations. Units freed from engagement before their Combat activation do not receive a replacement action. [RB pp. 55-56, 60, 67-68, 85; FAQ pp. 3, 6]

Table ruling U09: passing transfers the marker in Movement and Assault only. Retain it through Combat and end-of-round effects, then determine next-round initiative normally. Explicit card exceptions still apply.

Supply and reinforcement

Round 1 uses the Mission Card's starting Supply Pool; later rounds add escalation. The final round has unlimited Supply. At all other times:

Available Supply = Supply Pool - total Current Supply of friendly on-table units.

A deploying/summoned unit must fit the available capacity; losses immediately change Current Supply when a model-count bracket is crossed, freeing capacity. Reserves do not count toward on-table Supply. Use current brackets, not the original list's Supply, for on-table contests and applicable Disengage checks. [RB §§6.1-6.2, p. 44; §§8.3.1-8.3.3, p. 55; §11, pp. 83, 90]

topics.title: Movement & deployment
topics.html:
Measure, choose a leader, set followers

Premeasure freely. Measure horizontal base-to-base distance and ignore vertical height unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Within requires any part of a base in range; Wholly Within requires the entire base. A unit is Within if at least one model qualifies, and Wholly Within only if every model qualifies. Base-to-base means touching. [RB §§4.1-4.3, pp. 33-34; §11, p. 91]

For each repositioning action, nominate a Leading Model and measure its actual travelled path. Standard Move is up to Speed; no part of the leader's base may finish beyond the allowed distance. Set followers around its new position instead of measuring each follower's travelled path. Normally each follower must be Wholly Within 3 inches horizontally of the leader, with a continuous coherency link through the unit. Squadron changes that distance to 4 inches on its cards. Links cannot use another unit or an impassable route; terrain the leader could traverse, Access Points and the stated engaged-enemy exceptions can form valid links. Flying links ignore terrain/models. [RB §§4.4-4.6, pp. 35-37; §8.5.3, pp. 56-57; FAQ p. 3; Zerg Squadron cards]

If necessary, set followers as close as legally possible with a valid link beyond the distance: the unit is Out of Coherency and cannot contest. A model for which no legal linked position exists is removed. Deployment must put all models In Coherency or the location is invalid. Check coherency at the end of repositioning, not again merely because casualties broke the formation. [RB p. 35; FAQ p. 3]

Restriction Normal Ground movement
Models Leader can pass through its own unit, not other Ground units; Ground and Flying can pass through one another. Followers are set legally.
Terrain May cross Size 0/1, but cannot finish overlapping; cannot cross Size 2+ without an applicable exception or Access Point.
Gap clearance Leader Size 1/2 needs at least 1 inch; Size 3+ needs at least 3 inches between obstructing terrain/models. Include impassable High Ground edges. Final base must still fit.
End position Entire base on battlefield, no base overlap; an unengaged unit cannot end within enemy Ground Engagement Range except via an authorised rule.
Directly towards/away Follow the specified centre-line direction and shortest necessary obstacle detour, maximising the required movement; stop at the battlefield edge rather than leave it.

[RB §§4.5-4.6, p. 37; §§8.5.3-8.5.4, pp. 56-58; FAQ p. 3]

Elevation Definition and interaction
Ground Level On the play surface; distinct from the Ground combat tag.
Mid Ground On horizontal Size 1/2 terrain.
High Ground On horizontal Size 3+ terrain.
Access Point Agreed connection between elevations; normal units change level only here. Followers may link through it.
Ramp Size 1 Mid Ground, with an Access Point at each end; enter/exit at those ends, not across its side. May stop on it.

Ground Level cannot engage High Ground. Mid Ground can engage an adjacent level only when both models are adjacent to the same connecting Access Point. A base on multiple levels uses the highest. [RB pp. 48-49, 53, 57, 84-87; FAQ p. 3]

GRASS is special Size 2 terrain: it permits travel while blocking LoS under the normal cover tests. Remove it permanently if a leader's path crosses it or a model ends on it during the listed movement actions. Flying over it does not remove it; ending on it does. This removal is an exception to an ordinary terrain-overlap endpoint, not a rule that all Size 2 terrain can be traversed. [RB pp. 57, 85]

Deploy, Disengage, Run and Flying

Deploy brings a Reserve unit from an authorised Entry Edge, up to its allowed movement, subject to available Supply, legal bases and all-model coherency. It cannot finish within the opponent's Zone of Influence. Reserve units cannot first use Stimpack, Creep bonuses or other abilities unless expressly authorised while in Reserves. High Ground touching the edge can be an arrival surface; an Entry Edge on another level does not automatically extend to it. [RB §8.5.5, p. 58; FAQ pp. 3-4]

Table ruling U02: for normal entry, treat the Entry Edge as the starting footprint. Finish the leader's entire base within its Speed allowance of that edge, using a legal path and wholly on the board. Beyond a partial edge's endpoint, measure from that endpoint. Do not add a base diameter. Explicit alternative deployment abilities retain their own instructions.

Only the Deployment Card's primary Entry Edges generate Zones of Influence. Pylon/Omega Worm bases count as friendly Entry Edges for applicable abilities but do not create new Zones of Influence; ordinary forward-deployment abilities do not create Entry Edges. Pylon entry ends the deploying unit's activation, including further Active abilities. End-of-round indicator deployment requires leader base contact and coherent followers outside enemy Engagement Range; if blocked, it is wasted. 'Nominated to deploy' includes any effect making a Deploy action. [FAQ pp. 4-5]

An engaged unit must Disengage rather than make a normal Move. Move it clear of enemy Engagement Range. Remove individual models that cannot legally escape. If the leader cannot escape, remove it, leave the rest, end the failed activation. Normally that unit cannot shoot or charge in the following Assault Phase. It ignores this penalty if its Current Supply strictly exceeds the combined Current Supply of its engaged enemies when Disengage is declared, or an explicit ability waives it. Run is a further normal Speed move in Assault, not an automatic double-Speed move. [RB §§8.5.4, 8.6.3, pp. 57-60; TACTICAL MASS, p. 90]

Flying leaders move point-to-point over models and terrain and ignore elevation. Final positions still need legal, non-overlapping bases and must stay at least 1 inch from enemy Flying models. Flying units cannot engage, charge, be charged, fight in Combat, or control/contest objectives. For LoS/cover they count as larger than every terrain piece: ignore Full Cover, never receive Direct Cover or High Ground cover themselves; Direct Cover protecting another model and the Dead Zone rules still matter. [RB pp. 49, 58, 85]

topics.title: Attacks, cover & casualties
topics.html:
Line of Sight and cover

Trace LoS in 2D from any part of the acting model's base to any part of the target base. A usable trace makes that model Visible. Terrain footprint is its base or outermost solid edges viewed from above; windows, doors and open interiors inside that footprint block LoS by default unless the players agree otherwise. A standable surface beneath the models does not block their trace merely by supporting them. Effective Size is model Size plus supporting terrain Size; stacked terrain also adds its supporting Size. [RB §§7.1.1-7.1.3, pp. 45-52; §11, pp. 84, 86-87]

Situation Result
Full Cover A crossed terrain piece has Effective Size at least as high as both models: LoS blocked.
Direct Cover Trace crosses terrain, either model is Within 1 inch of that piece, and terrain is at least that nearby model's Effective Size: LoS blocked in both directions.
Close Quarters Both models Within 1 inch of the same piece and Within 3 inches of one another: ignore Direct Cover and the elevation/Dead Zone restriction; Full Cover can still block.
Elevation Dead Zone High Ground model cannot see a Ground Level model Within 1 inch of the base of the same terrain, and vice versa, unless Close Quarters applies.
High Ground cover Against ranged attacks: every defending model has some base on High Ground and at least one attacker is lower, granting Evade eligibility. Flying attackers are not lower for this purpose.

Check each terrain piece independently; do not combine separate pieces' Size or proximity into one blocker. Cover here usually blocks LoS; it is not a universal Armour bonus. High Ground's save is the stated exception. [RB pp. 45-52; FAQ p. 4 corrects the High Ground summary]

Ground units are engaged when eligible enemy Ground bases are Within 1 inch, provided intervening Size 2+ terrain and elevation do not prevent engagement. Size 0/1 terrain does not prevent it. One engaged model engages its entire unit. Flying units never engage. [RB §7.2, p. 53]

Ranged Attack and weapon batches

An unengaged unit normally cannot shoot an engaged enemy. An engaged unit normally shoots only enemies in its own engagement and cannot use BULKY weapons. PINPOINT allows shooting at engaged targets, not shooting out of your own engagement. INDOMITABLE permits its stated exchange with unengaged units, granting the defender Evade, but does not allow shooting into another engagement. [RB §8.7.3, p. 60; FAQ pp. 6-7; Goliath card, Terran base PDF p. 7]

The selected Queen has no INDOMITABLE ability. Her Ground-targeting Talons cannot shoot out of her engagement at an unrelated unengaged unit. [Zerg base PDF p. 5]

Each model uses one weapon for the phase, plus any SIDEARMs. Models using the same weapon profile combine into a batch and must target the same unit; each firing model needs an eligible enemy in range and Visible, unless its rule overrides LoS. Different weapon profiles and SIDEARMs are separate batches and may choose different legal targets. Declare and finish one batch before choosing the next; earlier casualties may change subsequent targeting. [RB §8.7.3, pp. 60-61; §11 SIDEARM, p. 89; FAQ pp. 4, 7]

Step Resolution
1. Attack Pool Sum eligible models' RoA, apply applicable dice modifiers; take one Surge die for the batch if the profile has one.
2. Hit Roll attack dice against modified Hit; successful dice enter the Armour Pool. Apply PRECISION to failed dice if available.
3. Surge If the target matches the Surge type, move that many successful hits directly to Damage, bypassing Armour. Cap at actual successful hits, then apply DODGE. CRITICAL HIT also bypasses Armour within the available pool.
4. Armour Defender rolls remaining Armour Pool against modified Armour; discard successes, move failures to Damage. TOUGH converts its allowed failed saves.
5. Evade Only if a rule grants eligibility, roll Damage Pool against Evade, including armour-bypassing hits; discard successes. A dash allows no roll.
6. Damage Multiply remaining dice by Dmg, or the matching PIERCE replacement. Add existing damage, apply applicable damage reduction, then remove casualties.

[RB §8.7.4, pp. 61-63; FAQ pp. 3-6; keyword entries pp. 82-90]

Surge and CRITICAL HIT do not create extra hits. PRECISION, CRITICAL HIT and similar numeric effects apply per weapon batch, not per model. No ordinary Damage resolution is created by a batch with no damage getting through; existing NON-LETHAL damage alone does not trigger casualties. [RB pp. 61-63, 83, 88; FAQ pp. 4, 6-7]

Damage, casualties, shields and healing

The defender chooses eligible casualties. Remove a model for each full HP amount in Total Damage, reducing the pool accordingly; leave any allowed remainder as the unit's Damage Marker. Shield increases the first model's HP only. For shooting an unengaged unit, only Visible models can die, regardless of whether those models were individually in the weapon's range. When the last Visible model is removed, discard remaining Total Damage instead of carrying it into hidden models. INDIRECT FIRE can remove non-visible models; its out-of-LoS Evade applies only if the target unit has no Visible model. [RB pp. 38, 62-63; FAQ pp. 4, 7]

For an engaged target use this order, without a LoS requirement: models outside all enemy Engagement Ranges first; then engaged models not in enemy base contact; then models in base contact. Do not remove a model that breaks an existing engagement with a particular enemy while another valid casualty remains, even across these priorities. [RB §8.7.4, p. 63; §12.7, p. 93]

SHIELDED is lost when Total Damage exceeds the Shield value, or the first model dies. Healing reduces damage in the combined HP pool but cannot restore SHIELDED. NON-LETHAL DAMAGE adds damage without removing models; subsequent ordinary damage can cause casualties using the combined pool. Non-lethal damage can remove SHIELDED. HEAL does not return dead models; RESPAWN is a separate rule and cannot increase the unit's Current Supply bracket. Damage reduction applies to the combined existing and newly suffered damage. CONCENTRATED FIRE discards all remaining combined damage after its casualty cap is reached. [RB pp. 38, 62-63, 83, 86, 88-89; FAQ pp. 3, 5, 7]

Charge

Only an eligible unengaged Ground unit charges. Declare every enemy target unit and choose a model in each before rolling Speed + d6. No LoS is required. The leader must reach Engagement Range of all declared targets, along a legal route, without engaging undeclared enemies. Table ruling U03: measure actual leader movement consistently within Speed + d6; neither add a free base diameter nor deduct an extra base diameter. On failure it stays put and its activation ends. [RB §8.6.2, pp. 65-66]

On success, place the leader in base contact if possible, otherwise as close as possible within engagement. Set followers prioritising base contact, then Engagement Range, then coherency. Do not create undeclared engagements. Resolve IMPACT immediately: each eligible Fighting/Supporting model generates the listed number of Impact dice; successes at the specified number are hits of Damage 1, with no Surge. HIDDEN is immune. IMPACT does not target a unit, which matters for Structure restrictions. [RB pp. 65-66, 86; FAQ p. 6]

Close Combat Attack

Every engaged unit must activate once in Combat. First it may Close Ranks: leader up to 3 inches, ending closer to an engaged enemy, followers set to maximise contact. Do not move base-contact models, break existing engagements, or engage new enemies. A unit entirely pinned in base contact cannot move. [RB §8.8.1, p. 67; FAQ p. 4]

Fighting models are Within 1 inch of an eligible enemy. Supporting models touch a same-unit Fighting model but are not themselves in enemy Engagement Range. Both ranks may attack; other models cannot. Use one Combat weapon plus SIDEARMs per eligible model. LoS is unnecessary. Allocate models' attacks among enemies they are eligible to fight. A shared weapon batch's keyword allowance is shared across split target pools, not duplicated; assign its single Surge die to one target before rolling. Resolve Hit/Surge/Armour and any specifically granted Evade, then the engaged casualty rules. Engagement itself does not grant Evade. [RB pp. 67-68; FAQ p. 7]

Blast and Flamer templates

For a Blast, position to cover as much of the chosen primary target model's base as possible. Its base is the target point for relevant traces. For a Flamer, put the narrow end flush against the attacker and aim at the primary target; trace from that attacker. Count bases even partly under the template, on the same elevation and with eligible tags; intervening Size 2+ blocking terrain prevents the relevant effect. [RB §8.7.6, pp. 64-65]

Batch Attack dice Surge
Main target Number of affected models, plus applicable RoA modifiers No Surge die: use affected main-target count as the Surge result if tags match, capped by successful hits.
Each other friendly/enemy unit Separate Spillover batch using its affected-model count No Surge; no offensive weapon keywords. Guardian Shield explicitly reduces each batch by one die.

Spillover needs at least one shared combat tag with the primary target and the same elevation. Ability templates without a physical primary model use the template's centre point as primary target; it has no tags, so no tag-match restriction, but the same-elevation condition remains. For those ability templates, Flying uses its physical base's elevation. Storm aligns template and token centre-to-centre. Token-centred areas such as Creep/Bile normally affect all elevations; do not transfer that rule to every template. [FAQ pp. 6-8; U06, U11]

topics.title: Abilities, resources & statuses
topics.html:
Timing and payment

Table ruling U08: Glial Reconstitution on ordinary Roach and Corpser costs 1 BM, correcting their printed 1 CP to match Vile and Zerg resources. This is an agreed typo correction, not publisher errata. The October mineral purchase cost is separate. [Zerg base cards PDF pp. 6-7, 9; RB p. 81]

Ability type When / frequency
Active Only the currently activated unit, immediately before declaring or after fully completing an action; once per named ability per unit per round unless REPEATABLE. Specific printed timing can override this window.
Passive Applies while its conditions hold and its unit is on the battlefield; no activation needed.
Reaction Exact printed trigger, not retroactively; at most one reaction per player per activation, and each named reaction once per unit per round unless REPEATABLE. Outside activations, FAQ gives a phase cap with an unresolved REPEATABLE interaction (U05).

Multiple differently named Active abilities are allowed if costs can be paid. Tactical Card Active abilities still need an active on-table unit. Merely performing an action through another unit's ability does not make a unit active. Unit-targeted abilities normally require range and LoS; Tactical Cards do not require LoS unless stated. Selecting and targeting are synonyms; proximity checks and setting a token/location are not automatically unit targeting. Resolve active player's simultaneous triggers first; outside activations the First Player Marker holder has priority. Each player orders their own simultaneous effects. [RB §§10.1-10.5, pp. 79-81; FAQ pp. 5-7]

Terran spends CP, Zerg BM, Protoss PE. Exhaust Ready cards face-down to pay an ability's full cost, or to use a printed ability when required; a card cannot fund both uses. Excess resources disappear immediately and cannot fund a later ability. Exhausted cards cannot use abilities until refreshed, including the Academy's otherwise non-exhausting reaction. An ability may be free but still obey activation, timing and frequency rules. Do not assume abilities work in Reserves unless their text expressly allows it. [RB pp. 79-81; FAQ p. 5]

Persistence and repositioning effects

End-of-round buffs remain active through resolving End of the Round effects, then expire during cleanup. Statuses persist until their specified removal; STAY IN PLAY is not a universal immunity to destruction. Start of the Round gives STATIONARY to units; any model moving, being moved or PLACED removes it. Hold is an action and can trigger an action-based status loss; passing is not. [RB pp. 54, 72, 79-80, 90; FAQ p. 6]

Tokens are physical Size 0 objects: move across them but normally cannot end overlapping. Markers are tracking aids and do not obstruct bases. DISPLACEMENT lets the leader finish overlapping the relevant token/model, then its controller sets that object in base contact or as close as possible. Cleanup removes ordinary tokens/markers except the specified persistent categories. A unit's destruction ends its ongoing effects and removes its created tokens unless an explicit rule keeps them; effects already applied to other units retain their stated duration. [RB pp. 53-54, 72, 83; Raven exception FAQ p. 6]

PLACE removes and sets the leader Wholly Within its specified distance, then sets followers in coherency; ignores gap/elevation travel, but requires legal endpoints. It cannot set within enemy Engagement Range except when allowed in Assault or by explicit card text. It removes STATIONARY. Returning to Reserves retains damage and equipment, suspends ordinary abilities, removes the specified nonpersistent tokens/markers and does not erase the unit's current activation record. SIEGE MODE is lost on return. [RB pp. 58, 88-89; FAQ pp. 3, 7]

SUMMON needs Supply and legal contact/coherency, outside enemy engagement and Zone of Influence. It cannot activate in the phase summoned; in later phases it activates immediately after its parent's activation, or normally if that parent is absent. MORPH replaces the specified models with a new unit in legal base contact, requires Supply, and gives the new unit a marker preventing activation for the rest of the round. Both original and morphed units' Supply losses award mission VP as clarified by FAQ. RESPAWN returns models in base contact without increasing Current Supply and cannot revive a Destroyed unit absent an exception. [RB pp. 76, 88-90; FAQ pp. 3, 7]

Status and faction essentials

  • BURROWED: also gains HIDDEN on entry and each round start; becomes Size 0; counts as Supply 0 only for Disengage checks; cannot contest/control. Can use abilities and may Deploy, Move, Disengage, Run, Hold or Close Ranks, but all those actions except Hold remove BURROWED/HIDDEN. Gets Evade if its characteristic permits. When engaged it must activate in Combat, may unburrow via a legal Close Ranks, then fight; without that it cannot attack. Other models can cross it but cannot end within its Engagement Range. [RB pp. 82-83]
  • HIDDEN: cannot be a ranged or LoS-requiring ability target beyond 4 inches; grants Evade if available and immunity to IMPACT. Location-based detection can affect it without directly targeting the unit. It is not Visible beyond 4 inches. Indirect Fire does not override the ranged-targeting ban; charges require no LoS and remain legal. See the reviewed U07 interpretation. [RB pp. 65, 86, 91; FAQ p. 7]
  • SIEGE MODE: forbids Move, Disengage, Run, Charge and Close Ranks; use only Siege Mode weapons, and those weapons only in that mode. [RB p. 89]
  • ON CREEP: friendly or enemy Ground Zerg within 6 inches of a Creep Tumor or Source of Creep qualifies; benefits come from the relevant card. Accelerating Creep checks at movement start and lasts for that move. Its flat bonus stacks with the Queen's purchased Creep Speed upgrade; that upgrade is not selected in our starting army. Two BUFF Speed effects use only the highest. Enemy Move, Deploy, Run, Charge or Disengage ending within 1 inch removes a Creep Tumor; PLACE does not. Do not add Close Ranks to that card's list. [RB p. 88; Zerg base cards PDF pp. 3, 5, 10, 14-15; FAQ pp. 5-7]

Other universal weapon/effect keywords and card-specific concepts are indexed in the glossary. Named card abilities retain their printed targets, costs and phase windows; a generic summary cannot replace those instructions.

topics.title: Objectives, scoring & victory
topics.html:
At Phase 4 control determination, a contesting unit must be on the battlefield, In Coherency, and have at least one model Within 3 inches of the marker, with LoS to it and on its elevation. Treat the marker as Size 0 for LoS. Flying and BURROWED units cannot contest. Sum eligible units' Current Supply, not model count. Higher total controls; a Supply 0 unit can control an uncontested marker. A tie does not change ownership. Control remains after leaving until the opponent reclaims it with a higher total; a claimed marker does not revert to neutral. Use a Faction Indicator to record ownership. [RB §8.9.1, pp. 69-71]

Deactivated Mission Markers can still be controlled; activation affects scoring as the mission states. Artefact Hunt's CLAIM is distinct from control and can be used by Flying/BURROWED units when that mission's conditions are met. In Supply Drop, determine marker activation before rolling for priority. [FAQ pp. 3-4; relevant mission cards]

Then both players score the Mission Card, including its permitted Supply-loss VP and objective timing. Perform the printed end check: a special winning condition wins outright; eliminating all enemy on-table models and Reserves ends play and grants the survivor +10 VP (winner wording UNCLEAR, U12); the final round ends under the final-score procedure. At the start of the final Scoring Phase, remaining Reserves are considered Destroyed and award the mission's VP. Highest final VP wins; apply a mission tiebreaker or draw if none. [RB §§8.9.2-8.10, p. 72; selected Mission Card; final-effect timing U04]

If play continues, resolve End of the Round effects, holder first, then cleanup: remove transient tracking pieces but retain Damage Markers, Mission Markers, ownership indicators and STAY IN PLAY pieces; refresh exhausted cards. Give the First Player Marker to the player with fewer VP, or roll off if tied. This player still chooses who starts each phase; it is not compulsory first activation. [RB §§8.9.4-8.9.6, p. 72; §8.3, p. 55]

topics.title: Edge cases & disputes
topics.html:
Situation Check
Last model dies Unit is Destroyed; cannot return without an explicit exception. Apply Supply/scoring and token/effect consequences. [RB p. 54; FAQ p. 3]
A casualty changes Supply Recalculate immediately, even mid-round; this can change deployment capacity, objective weight and future Disengage checks. [RB pp. 39, 44, 83]
A model dies behind cover Ordinary unengaged shooting cannot do this unless Visible; Indirect Fire and engaged casualty rules are exceptions. [RB pp. 62-63; FAQ pp. 4, 7]
Failed deployment formation Pick another legal location; do not deploy an Out of Coherency formation. [FAQ p. 3]
Null statistic General granted movement/save effects do not overcome the dash. [FAQ p. 3]
Two copies of an effect Distinct flat modifiers may stack, duplicate named abilities/keywords do not; keep highest numeric keyword. [RB pp. 79, 82; FAQ p. 5]
Competing simultaneous rules Active player first, otherwise holder first; a player's own effects resolve fully in their chosen order. [RB pp. 72, 80; FAQ p. 5]
Dispute cannot be settled quickly Core dispute procedure: roll off 2d6; winner decides this instance, then verify after the game. Record it as a temporary ruling, not verified rules. [RB §12.9, p. 94]

The conflict register preserves differences from quick-start, tutorial and competitive material so that their shortcuts do not silently change these procedures.

topics.title: Glossary: one-line definitions
topics.html:
Participants, cards, building and dice

Term Definition Source
Active Player Player currently acting; resolves their simultaneous triggers first. RB pp. 29, 80, 82
Controlling Player Player making decisions and rolling for a unit, model, token or card. RB pp. 29, 83
Friendly Belongs to you or your teammate; a unit is friendly to itself. RB p. 85; FAQ p. 5
Enemy Belongs to an opponent; friendly attacks need an explicit exception. RB p. 84
Model One miniature/base within a unit. RB p. 28
Unit Models sharing one Unit Card and acting together. RB p. 28
Base Rules reference for position, distance and contact; sculpted pose is irrelevant. RB pp. 28, 33
Wobbly Model Syndrome Agreement to mark a legal position when the model cannot safely stand there. RB p. 28; FAQ p. 3
Faction / race Allegiance chosen through a Faction Card; Terran, Zerg or Protoss and applicable sub-factions. RB pp. 29, 41, 73-74
Faction Card Army's allegiance, initial Army Slots, resource and printed abilities. RB pp. 41, 81
Faction Tags All allegiance tags on a selected card must be present on its Faction Card. RB pp. 84-85
Unit Card Unit statistics, weapons, tags, Supply, abilities and upgrade choices. RB pp. 38-39
Tactical Card Purchased army infrastructure/support card granting slots, resources and abilities. RB pp. 40, 81
Creep Card Zerg card defining its Creep effects and propagation instructions. Zerg base cards PDF pp. 14-15
Mission Card Defines scoring, starting Supply, escalation, length and special conditions. RB pp. 42, 77
Deployment Card Defines table dimensions, Entry Edges, Zones of Influence and objective positions. RB pp. 43, 77
Army roster / list Selected units, compositions, upgrades and cards with their costs. RB pp. 73-76
Open Lists / Closed Lists Full shared roster by default / hidden roster by mutual agreement, still disclosing deployed equipment. RB p. 76
Engagement scale Skirmish, Standard or Grand Battle size and budget framework. RB p. 73
Minerals Army-building budget for units and upgrades. RB p. 73
Vespene Gas Separate card budget, 10% of agreed mineral limit. RB pp. 73-74
Mustering / composition option Selecting a listed model-count option for a unit and paying its cost. RB p. 74
Army Slot Typed capacity consumed by a unit's starting Supply. RB pp. 74, 82
Core / Elite / Support / Air / Hero Distinct Army Slot types; unused types do not substitute for one another. RB pp. 40, 74
Combat role Card's descriptive role, distinct from its Army Slot. RB p. 39
UNIQUE Only one copy may be selected. RB pp. 41, 74, 81; cards
Upgrade Purchased unit modification; replacement entries remove the named original weapon. RB pp. 39, 75
SPECIALIST One nominated model carries this upgrade; different Specialist entries use different models. RB pp. 75, 89; FAQ p. 7
Draft Veto/selection process choosing Mission and Deployment Cards. RB p. 77; FAQ p. 3
Red / Blue affinity Printed objective colour association, not automatic control. RB p. 77
CP / BM / PE Terran command, Zerg biomass and Protoss psionic ability resources, respectively. RB p. 81; faction cards
Ready Face-up card available to fund or resolve its permitted abilities. RB pp. 81, 88

Keyword Defined rules shorthand; duplicate keywords do not stack, numeric versions use the highest. RB pp. 29, 82

Ground Combat Tag for ordinary ground units; separate from Ground Level elevation. RB pp. 83, 85

Actions, attacks and effects

Damage Pool Unsaved and armour-bypassing hits awaiting any Evade, then damage multiplication. RB p. 62

Total Damage Newly suffered damage plus existing marked damage, before applicable allocation/reduction. RB pp. 62-63; FAQ p. 5
Damage Marker Accumulated damage carried by a surviving unit; persists through cleanup. RB pp. 53, 62-63, 72
Casualty Model removed when damage or another rule requires it. RB pp. 62-63
Destroyed Unit Unit whose last model has been removed; cannot return absent an explicit exception. RB p. 54; FAQ p. 3
Blast Template / BT Area shape placed over a primary model, or as an ability specifies. RB pp. 64-65, 94
Flamer Template / FT Area shape with narrow end flush to the attacker, aimed at the primary target. RB pp. 64-65, 94
Primary / Main Target Unit/model anchoring an ordinary template's main batch, target point, tags and elevation. RB pp. 64-65
Target Point Primary target base for Blast; template centre for an ability with no physical primary target. RB pp. 64-65; FAQ p. 7
SPILLOVER Separate template batches against other affected units; no Surge or offensive weapon keywords. RB pp. 64-65, 89; FAQ pp. 7-8

BUFF [characteristic] (X) Improve that statistic by X until End of the Round; lower TN or increase numeric value. RB p. 82
BULKY Weapon cannot make ranged attacks while its unit is engaged. RB p. 82
BURROWED Size 0, HIDDEN and other burrow restrictions; no objectives, most permitted actions unburrow. RB pp. 82-83
BURST FIRE Y (X) Add X RoA for ranged attacks against targets Within Y inches of the firing model. RB p. 83
CONCENTRATED FIRE (X) Remove at most X models, then discard all remaining Total Damage. RB p. 83; FAQ p. 7
CRITICAL HIT (X) Move up to X available successful hits directly to Damage, bypassing Armour. RB p. 83
DEBUFF [characteristic] (X) Worsen the statistic by X until End of the Round; raise TN or lower value to minimum zero. RB p. 83
DISPLACEMENT A leader ending on this object causes its controller to set it in base contact or closest possible. RB p. 83
DODGE (X) Reduce capped Surge/CRITICAL HIT bypass by X, minimum zero. RB p. 84; FAQ p. 6
HEAL (X) Remove up to X marked damage; does not return dead models or SHIELDED status. RB p. 86; FAQ p. 3
HIDDEN Protects against distant targeting, grants eligible Evade and IMPACT immunity; see U07. RB pp. 86, 91
HITS X (Y) Generate X automatic hits in Armour Pool, Damage Y, without Surge. RB p. 86
IMPACT (X) Y After a successful charge, each eligible fighter/supporter rolls X dice hitting on Y+, Damage 1, no Surge. RB p. 86

LOCKED IN (X) Add X RoA when shooting a target with STATIONARY status. RB p. 87; FAQ p. 7
LONG RANGE (X) Extend range to X inches with -1 Hit beyond the normal profile range. RB p. 87

NON-LETHAL DAMAGE (X) Add X damage without immediate casualty removal; later normal damage can allocate the combined pool. RB p. 88
ON CREEP Ground Zerg Within 6 inches of a tumor/source qualifies for the applicable Creep rules. RB p. 88

PLACE (X) Remove/set leader Wholly Within X, then coherent followers; legal endpoint and engagement restrictions remain. RB p. 88

RESPAWN (X) Return up to X dead models legally in contact without increasing Current Supply. RB p. 89

For exact procedures, see rules-summary.md. UNCLEAR entries and interpretive boundaries are kept in open-questions.md. Accepted group agreements are recorded in table-rulings.md, including Glial Reconstitution's corrected 1 BM cost on Roach/Corpser (U08).

topics.title: Our table agreements (not publisher errata)
topics.html:
These five agreements settle play for this group while retaining the publication discrepancies in the research record. Use them in the play references where marked Table ruling. Specific card exceptions still apply. Revisit an agreement when relevant official errata appear; record any change rather than silently replacing it.

ID Accepted decision Scope / evidence
U01 Use the agreed terrain layout; treat contradictory piece counts as guidance. Setup choice. No exact corrected quota is asserted. Current first-game layout: cargo-yard map; not yet play-tested. RB p. 78.
U02 For normal Entry Edge deployment, treat the edge as the starting footprint. The leader's entire base must finish within its Speed allowance of that edge, following a legal path and wholly on the battlefield. For a partial edge, measure beyond its endpoint from that endpoint, not an imaginary extension. No extra base-diameter reach. Explicit alternative deployment abilities retain their own instructions. RB p. 58; quick-start p. 6.
U03 Measure the leader's actual charge movement consistently, with allowance Speed + D6. Add neither a free base diameter nor an extra base-diameter penalty. Use corresponding base points when measuring movement; a straight translation moves the front by the same distance as the back. Legal paths, clearance, engagement with all declared targets, and follower coherency still apply. RB pp. 56, 65-66.
U08 Glial Reconstitution costs 1 BM on ordinary Roach and Corpser, matching Vile. Agreed typo correction to their printed 1 CP. This is the activation resource cost; mineral purchase costs still use the October table. Zerg base cards PDF pp. 6-7, 9; RB p. 81.
U09 Passing transfers the First Player Marker in Movement and Assault only. Do not transfer it for passing in Combat. Retain it through end-of-round effects, then determine next-round initiative normally from VP or a tied-score Roll-Off. Explicit card exceptions still apply. RB pp. 55, 72, 85.

These two are sufficiently answered by existing publications; they do not require an additional house rule.

ID Clarification Evidence
U07 Beyond 4 inches, a HIDDEN model is not Visible and cannot be selected for ranged attacks, including Indirect Fire. A legal charge remains possible because it requires neither LoS nor ranged targeting. HIDDEN retains its Evade protection and IMPACT immunity. RB pp. 65, 86, 91; FAQ p. 7. Detection and other abilities follow their own targeting text.
U10 Each die can be rerolled once unless explicitly stated otherwise. Official quick-start p. 3; RB p. 31 does not expressly permit a second reroll. Invalid/cocked rolls and tied Roll-Offs have separate procedures.

topics.title: UNCLEAR: unresolved questions
topics.html:
The possible answers below have not been adopted. Agree an answer only if the selected cards or game situation require it.

ID Issue Possible answer / current status Confidence
U04 Artefact Hunt final scoring versus game-end check, RB p. 72; Protoss W2 PDF p. 5 The mission's final scoring must count. Proposed agreement: award it in final Scoring before comparing totals. Ordering against other End of Round abilities remains open. High that it scores; medium for proposed timing
U05 Outside-activation reactions: phase cap versus trigger cap, FAQ pp. 5, 7 Still UNCLEAR. One possible agreement is one per player per phase outside all activations; the alternative is treating REPEATABLE as a specific per-trigger exception. Neither is adopted. Older Reddit/fan answers do not resolve the current wording. Low for either universal interpretation
U06 Spillover and defensive modifiers, FAQ pp. 5, 8 Guardian Shield applies to every affected batch; weapon keywords do not carry into Spillover. Other modifiers need individual clarification; do not infer a blanket exception for every defensive modifier. High for the named rules; low for a general boundary
U11 Exact Blast/Flamer dimensions Equipment gap partly narrowed: an owner reports 4 15/16 inches, another commenter says 5 inches, and image-based guesses use 100-130 mm. These are separate community reports in their own units, not official dimensions. Exact diameter and Flamer outline remain unverified. Medium for approximate Blast size; low for exact size/Flamer
U12 Winner after elimination, RB p. 72 Likely add +10 VP to the survivor and compare totals. This makes the numerical bonus meaningful, but the book only expressly describes that comparison under round-limit ending. Automatic victory versus VP comparison remains UNCLEAR. Low for the inferred winner procedure

topics.title: A worked later-round shooting activation
topics.html:
This is an illustrative dice exercise, not a forced opening. Assume all six Marines B, armed with C-14 Rifles, can see and reach the fresh 12-model Zerglings B unit in open Ground Level within 12 inches. Neither unit is engaged; no buffs, cover, HIDDEN or other ability applies. [Marine card PDF p. 1; Zergling card PDF p. 10]

Step Example
Pool Six Marines x RoA 2 = 12 attack dice, plus one D3 Surge die for the whole batch.
Hit 3+ Results 1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 2, 1 give 8 hits.
Surge Separate d6 shows 3, read as D3 = 2; Zerglings are Light, matching the rifle. Move 2 hits directly to Damage; 6 remain for Armour.
Armour 6+ Rolls 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 save 1; the other 5 enter Damage.
Evade Zerglings have an Evade statistic but no eligibility here, so do not roll it.
Damage 2 bypassed + 5 failed saves = 7 dice x Damage 1 = 7 damage.
Casualties / Supply Remove 7 Visible Zerglings; 5 remain with no leftover damage. Supply drops 1 to 0, awarding Terran 1 Supply-loss VP in Frontlines.

[RB pp. 60-63; FAQ pp. 4, 6-7; Frontlines]

One colour should identify the Surge die. It moves successful hits past Armour; it never adds hits beyond the eight already rolled. If only three Zerglings had been Visible, ordinary shooting could remove only those three and would discard the remaining damage, rather than kill models behind the wall. [RB pp. 62-63]

topics.title: A charge and Combat follow-up exercise
topics.html:
Assume those five surviving Zerglings are later unengaged, with an unobstructed 6-inch legal route into the Marines, and a legal endpoint Wholly Within the rolled distance. Declare that Marine unit and one target model. Speed 4 + die 5 gives 9 inches, enough with margin. Set the leader and followers legally; only the declared enemy may become engaged. If all five Zerglings are Fighting/Supporting, Devastating Charge generates five IMPACT dice at 5+. Suppose two succeed: these are 2 Damage-1 hits, with Marine Armour saves before damage. For this exercise both Armour dice succeed on 5+, so no damage is caused. No Surge applies to IMPACT. [Zergling card PDF p. 10; RB pp. 65-67, 86]

In Combat, optional Close Ranks cannot move models already in enemy base contact. If all five remain eligible, their Shredding Claws contribute ten dice at Hit 4+. Zerglings B have no Adrenal Glands, so no Precision applies. Suppose six hit. Shredding Claws Surge against Light and Armoured; Marines are Biological, Light, Ground, so the Surge applies. A D3 result of 2 moves two hits past Armour; of the four remaining Marine Armour dice at 5+, suppose two save. The two bypassed plus two failed saves leave four Damage-1 dice: remove two 2-HP Marines. Four remain, still Supply 1, so no additional Supply-loss VP is gained. The Marines fight when selected if still engaged; only their Fighting/Supporting models contribute. [Marine/Zergling cards; RB pp. 63, 67-68]

topics.title: End-of-round objective exercise
topics.html: In Round 2, suppose Red retains marker 1 and takes marker 5 from Blue; Blue retains marker 2. Red scores 1 + (1 + 2) = 4 objective VP; Blue scores 1. Add that round's Supply-loss VP separately. A tie in Supply at marker 5 would have left Blue's previous ownership intact and given Red no recapture bonus. Check the 8-point lead condition after applying the mission's scores. [RB pp. 69-72; Frontlines Skirmish]
